To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the 3-fluid hydrodynamic model with the hadronic equation of states is capable of describing all available experimental data for the central Au+Au collisions at the AGS and SIS energies; (b) the same model is not able to describe the experimental data for the SPS and RHIC energies.

the 3-fluid hydrodynamic model, which uses purely hadronic equation-of-state (EoS) and is based on conservation laws of energy and momentum, reproduces the data from AGS, SPS and RHIC experiments very well.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the available experimental data from AGS, SPS and RHIC do not require assumption of a quark-gluqon phase transition in order to be reproduced.
there is no need to invoke a phase transition to quark-gluongluon plasma in order to explain the data from AGS or SPS.

the available data on the transverse-mass and pseudorapidity spectra of hadrons and on the elliptic flow of pions, protons and antiprotons, on the energy dependence of the inverse slopes of kaons and antikaons and on the energy dependence and the centrality dependence of the ratio of yields of kaons to pions, can be reproduced by 3-fluid hydrodynamic model with purely hadronic EoS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3-fluid hydrodynamic approach to heavy-ion collisions is able to reproduce a lot of experimental data, but it is not able to describe all the data.
3-fluid model of heavy-ion collisions with purely hadronic EOS is able to reproduce the bulk of available data from AG and SPS.
3-fluid hydrodynamic approach to description of heavy-ion collisions is quite successful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data from AGS, SPS and RHIC can be interpreted in a purely hadronic scenario, with no need of invoking a quark-gluonic phase transition.
the data on the transverse mass spectra can be reproduced without invoking a phase transition into the quark-gluonic phase, but that the data on elliptic flows cannot.
the 3-fluid hydrodynamic model with purely hadronic EoS is able to reproduce a lot of experimental data on heavy-ion collisions.
